title: WPMS/2347/2014 of Bhuwan Arya Vs Girish Chandra Mainali

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No.2347 of 2014
Bhuwan Arya & others
 ÖÖ. Petitioners
Versus
Girish Chandra Mainali
 ....Ö. Respondent
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for the respondent.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Petitioners before this Court are invoking its supervisory
jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India
against the concurrent judgments passed by the two courts
below.
 The dispute pertains to one-half of the appurtenant land
of house no.723 situated in Survey No.99/70 at Cantonment
area, Ranikhet, District Almora. The said house itself has
been erected on an area of 1900 square feet and the total
appurtenant land of the house is 0.448 acre, which is
equivalent to 19515 square feet. On 25.08.1977, this house
was purchased by the predecessors-in-interest of all the
petitioners, namely, Sri Vidya Sagar and his real brother
Shankar Lal, sons of Sri Ganga Ram; and the land, whereon
this house was erected as well as the afore-stated appurtenant
land, was taken on lease from the Union of India for a period
of 30 years on the annual rent of Rs.72.20 paise. On
1.2.1978, after almost five months of execution of such lease
deed, lessor Vidya Sagar and his brother executed a sale deed
of the house for consideration of Rs.9,000/-. On 17.2.1982,
one-half portion of this house was re-purchased by the
original leaseholders-Aryas from the respondent Girish Chand
Mainali.

2
 The dispute arose when Sri Mainali filed release
application on 14.5.1993 under Section 21(2) of the U.P.
Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act,
1972 in the Court of Prescribed Authority, not for one-half of
the house owned by him (Since Aryas were under tenancy of
one half portion of the house owned by Sri Mainali while on
other half, they themselves were in occupation as the owners)
but for the one-half of appurtenant land of the entire house.
Mr. Mainali also got the Map sanctioned on 16.9.1992 from
the competent authority of the Cantonment Board for further
construction of a new house on that land. This release
application was resisted by petitioners-Aryas and the same
could be adjudicated only on 3.10.2013, i.e. after more than
ten years, by the Prescribed Authority of Almora, whereby he
accepted the application for release of 8507.50 square feet of
land.
 Appeal no.9/2013, filed by Mr. Arya challenging the
judgment passed by the Prescribed Authority, also failed on
11.9.2014, but this time, the Appellate Court reduced the total
area of release bringing it down to 7957.50 square feet land.
So, challenging the judgments passed by both the courts
below, this petition now has been filed on the ground that both
the courts have not recorded their satisfaction, as envisaged
under Section 21(2) of the said Act.
 It was vehemently argued by learned counsel for the
petitioners that at the time of execution of sale deed on
1.2.1978, only the house was sold and this appurtenant land,
which was on lease, could not have been transferred, either by
way of sale or by sub-lease whatsoever, because this entire
land, including the house structure, was on lease from the
Union of India, and thus, only the house could be sold, but
the rights over this land could not be transferred in any
manner to Sri Mainali by Sri Vidya Sagar and his brother.

3
 This Court is in agreement with the petitionerís argument
only to the extent that one-half of the house structure could
be sold, but at the same time, it is unable to agree that no
rights were transferred on the appurtenant land by the sale
deed dated 01.02.1978. This is manifest by a meticulous
reading of language of the sale deed itself executed by Sri
Vidya Sagar and his brother. It discloses that all the rights,
including the house erected on the said land, were sold and
the possession was delivered to Mr. Mainali, with the further
clarification that Mr. Vidya Sagar and his brother will have no
objection if the leasehold rights are also applied for mutation
by the transferees on the entire appurtenant land
admeasuring 0.448 acre. This premise is further clarified in
the written sale deed executed on 17.2.1982 for half of the
house executed by Mr. Mainali again in favour of Mr. Vidya
Sagar. So, the intention is very much transparent that not
only the house or one-half of the house in the respective sale
deeds afore-stated was transferred, but the full leased land
and half of the house were transferred in the respective sale
deeds, albeit only the leasehold rights were transferred and
not the title because no party could have passed the title
rights since they themselves did not possess the same.
 Having regard to the entire facts of the case, as above, I
find that the judgments passed by the courts below are very
much sound and perfect and there is no infirmity at all
therein. Rather, the area for release has been ascribed only to
the tune of 7957.50 square feet out of the total half which
comes to the tune of 8807.50 square feet of land.
 The petition is bereft of any merit and is dismissed at the
threshold.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 15.10.2014
Rdang
